name: Nodexeus Technologies
tagline: We run the infrastructure that has to stay up.
description: Nodexeus builds and operates blockchain nodes, AI agent platforms and the web3 software around them, on a custom-built bare-metal platform we own top to bottom, not a resold cloud stack. That control is why deploys land faster than most managed cloud providers.

principles: specific beats vague: name the failure mode, not the fear
state limits honestly instead of overselling
short, declarative sentences over hedged ones
our infrastructure is custom-built, not off-the-shelf: say so plainly, backed by the mechanism or number that proves it
a blunt, even provocative claim is fine when it's true and specific: that's confidence, not hype
avoid: bold claims with nothing concrete behind them
em dashes in any post copy; use a period, comma, or colon instead
sampleQuotes: We run the infrastructure that has to stay up.
Anyone can rent you a server. The work is everything after.
Not a tarball and good luck.
We do not publish a blanket uptime guarantee, because one that covers every network and every hardware configuration would be worth nothing.
We didn't rent a cloud stack and slap a logo on it. We built the bare metal underneath it ourselves.
Most 'cloud platforms' are someone else's hardware with a markup. Ours is ours, which is why a deploy here beats theirs on speed.
No hypervisor tax, no noisy neighbors, no waiting on someone else's capacity plan: that's what owning the metal buys you.
Onboarding a new custom chain takes competitors weeks and a lot of your budget. We do it faster and for less, because we're not renting the hardware underneath it.
Run it in our data center or yours, on our hardware or your own. Same bare-metal performance, same automated updates, either way.

socialContentPillars: uptime and incident transparency (what broke, what we did)
AI agent and web3 engineering work in production
the bare-metal platform itself: why we built it and what it buys in deploy speed and performance vs. rented cloud
custom blockchain onboarding: faster and cheaper than competitors, and why
deployment flexibility: our data center, the customer's data center, or the customer's own hardware, all with the same bare-metal performance and automated updates

socialConventions.hashtags: platform-dependent: sparingly on X/LinkedIn, mainly to name a network or event; on Instagram, use them actively, since good hashtag use there drives real discoverability
socialConventions.emoji: none, or a single one at most
socialConventions.punctuation: no em dashes, ever; use a period, comma, or colon instead
socialConventions.postLength: 1-3 short sentences; threads only when reporting a real incident or upgrade in steps
socialConventions.cta: specific and low-pressure (e.g. 'ask us what that costs'), rarely hype-driven

onBrand: Base client update landed this week. We're on it across every base-mainnet node we run. No action needed if that's us.
Uptime numbers only mean something next to the incident that tested them. Ask us about the fork we caught at 3am last month.
New: private RPC endpoints for our newest supported network, same operating model as our Ethereum fleet. Talk to an engineer if you're evaluating providers.
Our platform is bare-metal, top to bottom, and we built it ourselves. No hypervisor tax, no noisy neighbors. Deploys land faster than most managed cloud stacks.
Standing up a new custom chain usually takes competitors weeks and a lot of your budget. We do it faster, for less, because we own the hardware.
Keep your nodes in your own data center if you need to. You still get bare-metal performance and the same automated updates as our fleet.
